note: ERRATA 54, and Q9 and Q14 as ruled. ONE DRAWN SIZE. Errata 24's two tiers, its decimation threshold and the eye_death_row measurement behind it are all void: errata 54 replaced decimation with ordinary filtered resampling, so there is nothing for a threshold to switch between. Frames are individual RGBA files in the per-clip directories under art/actors/, which is what the old sheet-and-cell schema could not address -- that was the blocking half of Q14. Generated by tools/build-actor-record.mjs from each directory's rig.json; do not hand-edit.
heightNote: MEASURED, and it replaces 205. That number came from reading Room 1's fence as chest-to-shoulder on a man -- an eye judgement treated as a measurement -- and it left the protagonist at 23.7% of the play area against Monkey Island's 27.8%. The wagon wheel is a second independent anchor and the two disagreeing is what exposed it. 240/864 matches. The room's curve is rescaled with its shape unchanged. Errata 54's original ~233 was arithmetic from Monkey Island's proportions and was never checked against the plate at all.
walkSpeedNote: 134 px/s, DOWN FROM 170, and the change is a consequence of walking becoming time-based rather than a retune of taste. The gait advances from DISTANCE, so while movement was frame-locked at a fraction of its declared pace the legs barely turned over and it read as a glide. Fixed, he covered the declared 245 px/s -- which over his measured 102px stride is 2.4 strides a second. A walking man does about 1.9, and 134 is exactly that. Actor.ts predicted this in its own comment before anyone could see it: "the legs now tell the truth about the speed, and the speed is a sprint." Hob keeps his ratio; he ambles on purpose. One number per actor if the pace wants changing again.
strideNote: MEASURED FROM HIS OWN FRAMES, never taken from Thad's -- R5f. The widest separation across his cycle is 230px in a 526px figure, which is 105 drawn pixels at height 240, or 0.44 of his height. His walk has the same structure as Thad's: eight frames, five distinct, ping-ponged.
idleBreakNote: Doc 40's idle-break, which the old record could not declare because it had no clip for it. Played on a timer while he is idle and returning to stand afterwards, never looped. 2/s over twelve frames is a six-second gesture.
